topic: Even if with true P: the reference to §14.1.1
claim: “As noted in §14.1.1, even if P may be used in a context where the truth of P is not in question”, with Even if you are my elder brother, you haven’t the right to tell me what to do.
evidence_summary: The point is made in §13.3, p. 737: “Even if may be used, however, in a context where the complement of if is known to be true”, with [15i] You don’t have to defend everything Ed does, even if he is your brother. In §14.1.1 (pp. 739–743) even if occurs only in [8i] (p. 741), on cancelling the only-if implicature. Page 749 repeats the pointer for “those cases considered in §14.1.1 where the truth of P is contextually given”, which then include the elder-brother example as [38ii] (p. 750).
finding: Medium confidence: the reference should be to §13.3. §14.1.1 does discuss conditionals whose P is established or self-evident (p. 742 [10]), and the p. 749 pointer is right for [38i] and [38iii], so the authors may have meant that general point. But the specific point about even if and its concessive reading is made in §13.3.
inference: Does §14.1.1 note that even if can be used when P is known to be true?

evidence.passage: §14.1.3, p. 748. “As noted in §14.1.1, even if P may be used in a context where the truth of P is not in question”
